steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-v2-without-qc-only-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 sample columns; first column holds gene identifiers — verify the column names against the sample IDs in metadata.csv, 12 rows x 2 columns with a condition column whose values are the treated/lesional vs control labels) and compute, per sample: raw total counts, log10 library size, median-of-ratios size factors (pydeseq2), CPM-normalized totals, and gene-detection counts at CPM > 1 and CPM > 5. Produce a per-sample QC table (CSV) and a barplot of library sizes (raw and size-factor-adjusted) highlighting sample_01, reporting its exact depth ratio to the median. caveats: With n=6 per arm, PCA separation by condition may be weak even when DE signal is real; do not interpret absent separation as absence of differential expression

A 4x-shallow library inflates its Euclidean distance to all others mechanically; the correlation-based distance and the sensitivity analysis exist to separate depth effects from expression-profile divergence
Salmon gene-level counts with unknown length-correction status are adequate for PCA/clustering QC but this caveat must be restated if these plots are later used to justify DE choices
steps.context: Same 12-sample AD skin dataset (6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch). PCA and distance metrics must run on within-sample-comparable values: log2-CPM, or VST if pydeseq2 provides it on 12 samples. steps.question: Do the 12 AD skin samples separate by condition (treated vs control) on PCA and cluster coherently by sample-to-sample distance, and is sample_01 a shallow-but-conforming sample or a structural outlier whose removal changes the picture?
constraints: PCA and distances use the top most-variable transformed genes; state how many genes were used and the transform applied
Report whether sample_01's condition is treated or control explicitly in the verdict — depth alone is not an outlier criterion without it
Do not exclude sample_01 or any sample from the primary analysis; removal appears only in the labeled sensitivity analysis
steps.description: Using the QC output of T1S1, transform the filtered counts to log2-CPM (and DESeq2-style VST via pydeseq2 if it runs cleanly on these 12 samples; otherwise log2-CPM alone, recording the choice), take the top ~500-2000 most variable genes, and compute: (a) PCA — PC1/PC2 loadings, per-sample scores colored by condition with sample_01 highlighted, and variance explained; (b) sample-to-sample Euclidean distance matrix on the transformed values with a heatmap and hierarchical-clustering dendrogram (correlation distance reported as a secondary metric); (c) a quantitative sample_01 assessment — depth ratio (from T1S1), detection-rate deficit vs its condition peers, transformed-profile correlation to every other sample, distance to the treated-group and control-group centroids, and its contribution/position on PC1-PC2 — plus a check that the shallow depth does not simply reflect a condition imbalance (state sample_01's condition); (d) sensitivity: recompute PCA and the distance heatmap with sample_01 removed and report whether condition separation and clustering conclusions change. Finish with a written verdict: whether sample_01 is flagged as an outlier (shallow-only, or shallow-and-divergent), whether any other sample looks anomalous, and what this implies for the upcoming treated-vs-control comparison — with the exclusion decision left to the user.
acceptance_criteria: PCA figure (PC1 vs PC2, colored by treated vs control, sample_01 annotated) with variance-explained percentages saved, computed on the top variable genes of log2-CPM or VST values (choice recorded)
Sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap plus hierarchical-clustering dendrogram saved; correlation-distance matrix reported
Sample_01 quantitative profile: depth ratio, detection deficit, nearest-neighbor correlations, distances to both condition centroids, and PC1/PC2 score vs condition centroid positions
Sensitivity PCA and distance heatmap without sample_01 produced, with an explicit statement of whether condition separation and sample clustering change

Written verdict text delivered: flag/no-flag for sample_01 (shallow-only vs shallow-and-divergent), any secondary outliers, and implication for the treated-vs-control DE comparison; no sample is actually excluded in this run

plan.title: AD skin RNA-seq: QC, PCA, distances, shallow-sample verdict
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a pre-test QC readout of the 12-sample atopic-dermatitis skin dataset (6 treated/lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, 12,000 gene-level Salmon counts). No differential testing is done. Step 1 quantifies library depth and gene-detection behavior per sample, establishing how far sample_01 falls below the cohort (profile flags it at ~4x below median library size) and whether median-of-ratios size factors correct it. Step 2 transforms counts for visualization (log2-CPM, with DESeq2-style VST if available), then produces the PCA, the sample-to-sample distance heatmap and clustering, and a quantitative outlier assessment of sample_01 — depth ratio, detection-rate deficit, distance to condition-group centroids, PCA leverage — plus a sensitivity PCA with sample_01 removed. The output is descriptive QC evidence and an explicit verdict; exclusion of any sample remains a user decision taken before DE testing.
